===== KStars Ekos Mount, DBus method documentation
Source : kstars/ekos/mount/mount.h, mount.cpp, kstars/indi/indistd.h
Repo   : https://invent.kde.org/education/kstars
         (read through the GitHub mirror https://github.com/KDE/kstars)
Commit : 61d849b04c42217cf2f0ab956153e56a928ae8a8
         the ref scripts/install.sh pins as KSTARS_REF, tag stable-3.8.3
Fetched: 2026-08-23

Why this file exists
--------------------
kstars-dbus-interfaces.xml and kstars-ekos-running.xml record that
org.kde.kstars.Ekos.Mount.slew takes two doubles named RA and DEC. They do not
record what those doubles mean. DBus has no notion of units, so a right
ascension sent in degrees is accepted by the signature and points the telescope
somewhere else entirely — the failure mode issue #2 exists to prevent, in a
place introspection cannot reach.

And in one case the XML is not merely silent but WRONG. See part 2.

Part 1 — the slew and sync family, verbatim from mount.h
--------------------------------------------------------
        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Slew the mount to the RA/DEC (JNow).
             * @param RA Right ascention is hours.
             * @param DEC Declination in degrees.
             * @return true if the command is sent successfully, false otherwise.
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool slew(double RA, double DEC);

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Slew the mount to the target. Target name must be valid in KStars.
             * @param target name
             * @return true if the command is sent successfully, false otherwise.
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool gotoTarget(const QString &target);

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Sync the mount to the RA/DEC (JNow).
             * @param RA Right ascention is hours.
             * @param DEC Declination in degrees.
             * @return true if the command is sent successfully, false otherwise.
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool sync(double RA, double DEC);

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Sync the mount to the target. Target name must be valid in KStars.
             * @param target name
             * @return true if the command is sent successfully, false otherwise.
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool syncTarget(const QString &target);

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Get equatorial coords (JNow). An array of doubles is returned. First element is RA in hours. Second elements is DEC in degrees.
             */
        Q_SCRIPTABLE QList<double> equatorialCoords();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Get Horizontal coords. An array of doubles is returned. First element is Azimuth in degrees. Second elements is Altitude in degrees.
             */
        Q_SCRIPTABLE QList<double> horizontalCoords();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Get Horizontal coords.
             */
        Q_SCRIPTABLE SkyPoint currentTarget();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Get mount hour angle in hours (-12 to +12).
             */
        Q_SCRIPTABLE double hourAngle();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Get the hour angle of that time the mount has slewed to the current position.
             * This is used to manage the meridian flip for mounts which do not report pier side.
             * only one attempt to flip is done.
             */
        Q_SCRIPTABLE double initialHA();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Aborts the mount motion
             * @return true if the command is sent successfully, false otherwise.
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool abort();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Get the mount slew status ("Idle","Complete", "Busy", "Error")
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE IPState slewStatus();


        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Get the mount slew rate index 0 to N-1, or -1 if slew rates are not supported.
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE int slewRate();

        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool setSlewRate(int index);

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Reset mount model if supported by the mount.
             * @return true if the command is executed successfully, false otherwise.
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool resetModel();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Can mount park?
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool canPark();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Park mount
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool park();

        /** DBUS interface function.
             * Unpark mount
             */
        Q_INVOKABLE Q_SCRIPTABLE bool unpark();

        /** DBUS interface function.

Part 2 — setMeridianFlipValues, where the XML's argument name is wrong
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The adaptor XML in kstars-dbus-interfaces.xml declares:

        <method name="setMeridianFlipValues">
            <arg name="activate" type="b" direction="in"/>
            <arg name="hours" type="d" direction="in"/>
            <annotation name="org.freedesktop.DBus.Method.NoReply" value="true"/>
        </method>

The argument is named `hours`. It is in DEGREES. From mount.h:


        /**
         * @brief set meridian flip activation and hours
         * @param activate true iff the meridian flip should be executed
         * @param degrees angle past the meridian when the flip should be delayed
         */
        void setMeridianFlipValues(bool activate, double degrees);

The brief says "hours", the @param says "degrees", the parameter is named
`degrees`, and the implementation in mount.cpp puts it straight into a widget
called meridianFlipOffsetDegrees:

    void Mount::setMeridianFlipValues(bool activate, double degrees)
    {
        executeMeridianFlip->setChecked(activate);
        meridianFlipOffsetDegrees->setValue(degrees);
    }

and meridianflipstate.cpp divides by fifteen when it uses it, which settles the
question beyond argument:

    // get the time after the meridian that the flip is called for (Degrees --> Hours)
    double offset = rangeHA(m_offset / 15.0);
    ...
    hrsToFlip = offset + getFlipDelayHrs() - ha;

So the offset is an HOUR ANGLE IN DEGREES, positive west of the meridian, and
the flip fires when the mount's hour angle reaches it. Sending 1.0 meaning "one
hour past the meridian" configures one degree — four minutes — instead.

Part 3 — ISD::ParkStatus, from kstars/indi/indistd.h
-----------------------------------------------------
The `parkStatus` property is declared as a bare `i`, annotated only with the
Qt type name. The values are:

    typedef enum { PARK_UNKNOWN, PARK_PARKED, PARK_PARKING, PARK_UNPARKING,
                   PARK_UNPARKED, PARK_ERROR } ParkStatus;

PARK_PARKED is 1. PARK_UNKNOWN is 0, and it is what the property reads before
the driver has reported anything, so it must never be treated as parked.

Part 4 — the catalogue lookup, from kstars/kstarsdbus.cpp
-----------------------------------------------------------
getObjectPositionInfo(objectName) returns a document whose coordinates are in
DEGREES, while Mount.slew takes RA in HOURS. The same factor of fifteen, at the
other end of the same operation:

    stream.writeTextElement("AltAz_JD", QString::number(data()->ut().djd(), 'f', 3));
    stream.writeTextElement("RA_Degrees", QString::number(target->ra().Degrees()));
    stream.writeTextElement("Dec_Degrees", QString::number(target->dec().Degrees()));

Two further consequences worth having in writing:

  - AltAz_JD is KStars' own clock, and it is printed to three decimal places of
    a Julian day. That is a resolution of 86.4 seconds, which is the floor under
    limits.targeting.resolver_max_clock_skew_s.
  - The name is looked up with data()->objectNamed(), and Mount::gotoTarget uses
    skyComposite()->findByName() — the same in-process catalogue. gotoTarget is
    literally a lookup followed by slew:

        bool Mount::gotoTarget(const QString &target)
        {
            auto object = KStarsData::Instance()->skyComposite()->findByName(target, false);
            if (object != nullptr)
            {
                object->updateCoordsNow(KStarsData::Instance()->updateNum());
                return slew(object->ra().Hours(), object->dec().Degrees());
            }
            return false;
        }

getObjectDataXML(objectName) returns the same coordinates plus the object type:

    stream.writeTextElement("Type", target->typeName());

Both return the literal string "<xml></xml>" for a name they cannot resolve.

What Nocturne takes from this
-----------------------------
- slew(RA, DEC) and sync(RA, DEC): RA in HOURS, DEC in DEGREES, frame JNow
  (equinox of date). The same units and frame as INDI's EQUATORIAL_EOD_COORD
  and as nocturne.safety.sky.SkyPosition, so no conversion happens anywhere.
- equatorialCoords reads back in the same units, in the same order.
- The bool every one of them returns means "the command is sent successfully",
  not that the mount accepted it and not that the motion finished.
- setMeridianFlipValues takes DEGREES. Nocturne names its argument offset_deg.
- getObjectPositionInfo returns DEGREES. Nocturne divides by fifteen at that
  boundary and nowhere else.
- parkStatus == 1 means parked. Nothing else does.
